subject: Insurance-first proposal for model-output indemnity (Order Form)
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@neptune-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@neptune-analytics.com>, Legal <legal@neptune-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Model-output indemnity — proposed insurance-first approach

Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is working through the Order Form redlines and we have one open item around indemnity for model-generated outputs. Attached is our redline (Neptune-OrderForm-Redline_v3.docx) and a short checklist of evidence we would expect in a third-party claim (Evidence-Req-Checklist.pdf).

High level: we cannot accept open-ended vendor liability for alleged IP infringement caused by the model output. Instead, we propose an "insurance-first" approach: Redwood would maintain commercial general liability + cyber/tech E&O limits, and Neptune would rely on those insurance policies for recovery against third-party claims arising from model outputs. We still expect Redwood to:
- take commercially reasonable steps to investigate and remediate claims;
- preserve logs/evidence as requested;
- reimburse direct damages if negligence can be established beyond reasonable doubt.

We can share procurement's target limits during a call. Can Redwood confirm whether an insurance-first approach is acceptable and what limits Redwood's carriers currently provide for tech/E&O? Also please confirm whether Redwood will accept our proposed evidence checklist and a 10-business-day acknowledgement SLA for notice.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Legal Operations
Neptune Analytics

Attachments: Neptune-OrderForm-Redline_v3.docx; Evidence-Req-Checklist.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Model-output indemnity — proposed insurance-first approach

Ben / Kim — forwarding Neptune's redline. Short summary: customer wants to avoid vendor indemnity for model-generated output and move to insurance-first, with an evidence checklist and a 10-business-day notice ack SLA. They do leave a small path for reimbursement if we are clearly negligent.

Questions for legal / sales:
- Kim: are we willing to accept insurance-first for model outputs in lieu of broad indemnity? If so, what guardrails do we need (e.g., carveouts, cooperation language, notice timing, evidence standards, insurance minimums)?
- Ben: commercial impact — would accepting this materially change pricing or SLA concessions? Could be a negotiation lever (we could offer insurance-first for hosted, but not for Dedicated/Private).

I added Marissa since she handles MSA/order form orchestration. I think a 30-minute call with Neptune procurement might close this quickly.

—Monica

Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model-output indemnity — proposed insurance-first approach

Monica / Ben — thanks for flagging. Quick legal take after reviewing Neptune's redline and the evidence checklist:

1) Insurance-first is acceptable as a commercial compromise, provided we secure:
   - a carveback so insurance applies only to outputs generated using Redwood-hosted models (i.e., not customer-provided models hosted in Dedicated/Private),
   - an explicit limitation that the insurance remedy is primary for alleged infringement claims arising directly from model outputs, while indemnity for defects in our code/SDKs or deliberate data misuse remains.

2) Notice & cooperation: 10 business days to acknowledge receipt is fine; we should require notice to include a reasonable evidence summary (what specific output, timestamps, customer prompts) before we are required to preserve broader datasets.

3) Defense control: we should resist mandatory defense control. Offer Redwood the right to participate and, if insured, to appoint counsel subject to conflict rules. If customer insists on defense control, require split of control only where customer pays for incremental costs beyond standard defense.

4) Caps & exclusions: propose a per-claim cap tied to the Order Form value or a € / $ amount (e.g., $5M) for model-output claims, with a carveout for willful misconduct.

5) Evidence handling: accept Neptune's checklist but add language limiting discovery to the specific KV/prefix cache relevant to the alleged output; we should avoid wholesale snapshot demands.

I'll attach a short redline snippet for an Order Form clause that implements the above. If Sales wants to offer this only for Hosted, we should include language excluding Dedicated/Private from the insurance-first path.

—Kim

Attachment: redline-proposed-clause.txt

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 13:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model-output indemnity — proposed insurance-first approach

Team — appreciate the quick turnaround. Commercial POV: Neptune is a mid-market account with steady predictable usage; switching to an insurance-first position could be an acceptable commercial concession if we:
- limit the approach to Hosted tier (we should not extend to Dedicated or Private deployments),
- require minimum insurance limits (we should ask for evidence of carrier limits and an endorsement naming Redwood as additional insured for the claim category),
- preserve the ability to fallback to traditional indemnity for software defects or for outputs produced using customer-uploaded proprietary training data.

Negotiation plan:
1) Offer the insurance-first language for Hosted only.
2) Ask Neptune to start with 3M USD E&O / tech policy limits and provide carrier summary. If they push back, we can propose 1M with an escrow cap tied to ARR.
3) Propose a short 30-min call (procurement + legal) to walk through the checklist and confirm what evidence they need so we can craft a targeted preservation scope.

Monica — want me to propose times? I can also offer a small commercial sweetener (60 days credit) if they agree to Hosted-only carveout and the 3M limit.

—Ben

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@neptune-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@neptune-analytics.com>, Legal <legal@neptune-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model-output indemnity — proposed insurance-first approach

Monica / Ben / Kim — thanks for the clear responses. Procurement discussed with our legal and they're generally open to Hosted-only insurance-first with the following asks:
- minimum E&O limit: 2M USD (we can accept your 1M counter if Redwood provides an escrow equal to 6 months of expected fees),
- Redwood must commit to preserve the specific prompt and output (and associated request id / timestamp) for 30 days upon notice; wider log requests will be scoped by a forensic review protocol, not automatic snapshotting,
- defense control: Neptune prefers to retain defense control but will accept joint control if Redwood reimburses material incremental defense costs beyond the insurer's standard counsel.

We can do a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT to finalize — I'll send a calendar invite if that works. If we agree on Hosted-only + 2M limit + 30-day preservation + joint control cost-share, procurement will greenlight.

Appreciate the willingness to find middle ground.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Legal Operations
Neptune Analytics
